SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

12. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

13. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

14. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

15. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

16. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water always increases oxygen

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
